label: input token c in the original phase
explanation: A single-token detector. It fires on every step where the input is the letter c during the original (pre-<DEL>) phase, and essentially nowhere else: no other input token, never at the delimiter, and almost never in the copy phase, even when c is fed back as an input there (109 tiny activations around 0.01-0.03 of max at recall_idx 1). Activation rate on original-phase c is about 100% at every position and for every L. Magnitude depends on position and repetition: it is strongest early in the sequence (the top examples are c at t=1, about 1.0 of max) and falls off at later positions (around 0.2-0.6 at t=6-8). It is also weaker on a repeated c than on the first c (e.g. 0.60 vs 1.00 in the same sequence).

issues: Minor: the magnitude story leaves something out. All of the top 1.00 examples are 'r c' at t=1, so peak magnitude may also depend on the previous token, not only on position. This does not affect the firing predicate.

Minor: I could not confirm the repeated-c weakening by scoring. The predicate with n_seen(['c'])==0 added gave exactly the same scores as the base predicate, so that helper may not be separating first from repeated c. The claim rests only on examples (1.00 followed by 0.60 in the same sequence).
Copy-phase leakage checks out: 109 dev and 90 test missed activations, all c fed back at recall_idx 1 at about 0.00-0.04 of max, holding 0.0% of activation mass. This is negligible.
